column1: # Column -> struct offset for every runtime table, from the 56 DB_Bind__<TABLE>
# binders. Per binding the compiler emits, before a std::map lookup:
#     mov  DWORD PTR [esp+0xdc],0x66      ; the STRUCT OFFSET
#     mov  DWORD PTR [esp+0x20],0x2       ; the key's value
#     call 0x862e40                       ; lower_bound on the table's own container
# THE OFFSETS ARE VERIFIED TWO WAYS. They were extracted from the Ghidra
# decompilation and then again from raw disassembly, paths sharing no failure
# mode, and all 50 tables the assembly covers came out IDENTICAL -- 403 offsets.
# The other 6 are single-column binders, settled by sibling agreement: all six
# Controls, all exact: _CHAR Strength 0x74 and RemainHwanCount 0x86 (both
# recovered independently by earlier rounds), PosX/PosY/PosZ 0x98/0x9c/0xa0, and
# _SiegeFortress FortressID 0x18 / Introduction 0x38 -- the last two added
# because the _CHAR controls passed while two successive parses were wrong.
# THE FOURTH COLUMN WAS WITHDRAWN IN ROUND 311. Rounds 308-310 published a
# `code` beside each offset and called it an uninterpreted per-column datum. It
# is not per-column data at all: EBX is pointed at that slot, and the callee
# dereferences EBX as a lookup KEY, comparing it against each node's key. So the
# integer selects an entry in the table's own container -- each binder uses a
# 0xd2109c) -- and the binder then uses the found entry's +0x48.
# Worse, the published values were often the WRONG SLOT: for _CHAR the real key
# slot is 0x20, while the decompiler's second variable was 0x2c. A corrected key
# column could only be recovered for 26 of the 50 binders (the compiler keeps
# EBX live across some bindings), so rather than publish a half-aligned column
# it is removed. Known about the key: small (0..11) and REPEATING -- 29 of 50
# tables reuse a key -- so it is neither a column ordinal nor a unique id.
